decision: Snapshot-staleness sweep 2026-09-17: canonical SFS (hard) on Qwen at 8 QPS x 16,000 requests, with the router acting on engine snapshots delayed by a fixed one-way delay D of 25, 100, 400 and 1000 ms (--snapshot-staleness-ms, a router-side delay buffer in the shared SHM snapshot transport; engines publish at their normal cadence, the simulator and SFS decision logic are unchanged). The same flag-gated remaining-length rule as the SFS/SCORE overlay is ON for qwen3-0.6b only, so each cell differs from the canonical qwen-hard-8 cell by D alone.

comparator.note: The D = 0 comparator is the canonical qwen-hard-8 cell of the sfs_score overlay (same policy, rate, budget, remaining-length rule and source lineage); this sweep adds no D = 0 cell. Compare each stale cell against that cell's point.json, not against another stale cell. A pool runs all four cells in one qualification: the smoke runs once at D = 0 and once at D = 1000 ms, and the completed-ledger entry of every cell records its D together with the sweep's level list.

worker.semantics: Every snapshot read on the router returns the newest engine snapshot whose publication timestamp is at least D ms older than now; the router keeps a small ring of recent publications per engine and serves what a network with D ms one-way delay would have delivered. Before any snapshot that old exists (startup) the oldest available is served and flagged (snapshot_delivery_fallback). Per request, wait_time_metadata records snapshot_staleness_ms, snapshot_delivered_version, snapshot_delivered_age_ms and snapshot_delivery_fallback; point.json config and the run record carry snapshot_staleness_ms.
worker.command: python -m scripts.cloud.worker campaign --bundle <bundle> --models <models.json> --state <state> --output <output> --family qwen --gpus <4 gpu ids> --campaign scripts/cloud/staleness-sweep-campaign-20260917.json --cells qwen-hard-8-stale25,qwen-hard-8-stale100,qwen-hard-8-stale400,qwen-hard-8-stale1000

remaining_length.note: Identical to scripts/cloud/sfs-score-campaign-20260917.json so the stale cells and the canonical comparator share the per-engine rule: only the qwen3-0.6b server receives the running_all/q0.5/prompt_bin rule; qwen3-8b, qwen3-32b and Ministral stay on the current rule. The rule is per engine: only the qwen3-0.6b server receives --remaining-length-mode running_all --remaining-length-table qwen3-0.6b.json --remaining-length-quantile 0.5 --remaining-length-conditioning prompt_bin, and the router attaches that table for its missing-prediction fill on that instance only. qwen3-8b and qwen3-32b stay off: reserve-tail-20260916 README sections 4.2/4.3 (8B target component within noise, hindsight replay worse under every candidate; 32B sub-second either way). Ministral stays off: no Ministral paired evidence (reserve-tail-ministral-20260917 is analysis only), the rule is only plumbed for the Qwen family and scripts.cloud.pool refuses it for a Ministral server. Tables were built from the calibration outputs only (zero overlap with the 16,000 evaluation ids); manifest.json records the build paths on the controller.

evidence.paired_run: scripts/cloud/reports/reserve-tail-20260916/paired-qps8p6-on/result_summary.json (Vast /workspace/sfs/state/diagnostics/reserve-tail-20260916/paired-qps8p6-on; canonical 8.6 QPS hard control, 16,000 requests, source bedeec4 + reserve diff)
evidence.reading: ON exceeds the better OFF control on both acceptance metrics (attainment 90.89 vs 63.71 percent; Pro OnTimeUtility 0.4732 vs 0.3561), outside the 13.8-point OFF spread; the pre-registered reading rule in the readiness note therefore admits the 0.6B rule for the campaign.
